name: Jewish Autonomism
summary: Jewish Autonomism, Simon Dubnow's doctrine, holds that the Jews are a living nation of a spiritual, cultural-historical kind that survived the loss of state, land and common language, and that in the Diaspora they should seek not a territory of their own but national-cultural autonomy inside the multinational states where they live. Its chief axiom is that Jews hold all citizens' rights both as individuals and as members of their nationality: secular, democratically run communities, their own schools and freedom of language, together with full civic and political equality. It rejects assimilation as national suicide and political Zionism's state as a messianic fantasy, while welcoming Palestine as one spiritual centre, puts national politics above class politics, and ties Jewish emancipation to a democratic constitutional order.
scope: Simon Dubnow's autonomism, which the Encyclopaedia Judaica (s2) says he named in 1901 and Pinson's essay (s7) presents as his national theory: the Letters on Old and New Judaism (1897-1907), including the Folkspartei programme he set out in the Twelfth Letter, read in the English edition Nationalism and History (s6), and his later programmatic letter of 1939 (s8). The Bund's socialist version, the Sejmists, Austro-Marxist personal autonomy, American diaspora nationalism (Janowsky, Kallen) and the Folkspartei's later Polish and Baltic branches are other subjects and are not used; nor is the unrelated autonomist Marxism.

sources.usedFor: Dubnow's last programmatic letter: fight against Nazi expulsions and closed immigration gates, boycott and armed participation against the Axis, emancipation without assimilation, free competition of ideas, no return to the ghetto.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Thirteenth Letter wants Jewish emigrants in America organised on a broad basis of national autonomy that protects them against cultural assimilation, which it calls the greatest danger there.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Dubnow founded the Folkspartei as a party and holds that political, social and class parties can and must exist within the nation, each subordinate to national survival.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Dubnow holds that every age devises its own forms of autonomy and that in an evolving Judaism new forms are adopted and old ones discarded.

class-collaboration.rationale: Dubnow accepts the workers' struggle with capital as natural within set limits, yet calls on Jews of all classes to unite and condemns leaders who teach Jewish workers to hate their own 'bourgeois' brothers; the Letters point both ways.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Eleventh Letter holds that the class struggle is one factor but not the only or even the most important one, and the Tenth rejects historical materialism in its absolute form; Pinson notes that Dubnow rejected the class interpretation of history.

clerical-rule.rationale: Dubnow wants the old synagogue community, centred on rabbis, replaced by free people's communities run by elected councils on democratic principles.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Dubnow's nationalism claims no territory for a nationality that is nowhere a majority, and Pinson records his opposition to national expansionism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Fourth Letter calls national autonomy an inalienable right of each nationality against the principle of a ruling nationality and wants its limits fixed by law and international law, beyond a majority's reach.

culture-before-state.rationale: Pinson quotes Dubnow that Zionism is healthy only if the return to Judaism is its primary goal and not merely an indirect aim of the return to a Jewish state.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Dubnow bases his nationalism on the equal worth of all nations, yet ranks national types from the lowest tribal stage to the highest spiritual one; his texts point both ways.

democracy-best.rationale: The Twelfth Letter calls a democratic regime the precondition of Jewish emancipation, and the Tenth sees a strong basis for the struggle against antisemitism only in the road to freedom that democracy provides.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Eleventh Letter calls the slogan of the dictatorship of the proletariat part of a confused Marxist policy, and the Twelfth makes a democratic constitution with equal rights for all citizens the precondition of everything else.

direct-action.rationale: The Twelfth Letter says every paragraph of the programme must be fought for first in the legislative assembly and then locally, and the Tenth wants a national group elected to the Duma, though Dubnow also backed Jewish participation in the 1905 revolution.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Fourth Letter blames the turmoil of multinational states on the suppression and forced assimilation of minorities and says peace and security require giving every nationality a measure of autonomy.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Pinson notes that Dubnow opposed the Zionists for their exaggerated sense of national mission and of being a chosen people, and the Third Letter grounds nationalism in the equal worth of all nations.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Dubnow condemns the tsarist policy of taking the Jews' livelihood from them and calls the hostility to free Jewish competition in commerce and industry a new antisemitism to be fought.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Dubnow wants the limits of each nationality's legal autonomy clearly established by law and firmly recognised in international law, and the programme seeks civic and national rights under a democratic constitution.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Second Letter holds that demanding Jews give up their nationality for equal rights contradicts the very concept of equal rights and the equal value of all men.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dubnow holds that history moves toward multinational states and calls the principle of a ruling nationality, 'cuius regio, eius natio', a political falsehood bound to be discarded.

gradual-change.rationale: The Fourth Letter counts every school and institution as a step toward the goal, but the Twelfth rejects winning rights piecemeal and the Thirteenth hopes to reach the immediate aims only in fifty years; the Letters go both ways.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Fifth Letter wants the school made an instrument of nationalisation so that pupils acquire universal culture through the national channel, and the Fourth counts every circle for Hebrew and Jewish history a step toward the goal.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Tenth and Thirteenth Letters want Palestine built as a spiritual centre for a Diaspora that will never vanish, though Dubnow also said he would gladly move the whole Diaspora to a Jewish state if that were possible.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Pinson notes that Dubnow had no feeling for mystical associations of a people with its land, and the Letters hold that the Jews survived as a nation after losing their land.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The chief axiom of autonomy in the Fourth Letter is that Jews hold all citizens' rights not merely as individuals but also as members of their national groups.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Tenth and Twelfth Letters call for a formal national organisation: a political league, a party, elected community councils and a Union of Jewish Communities with central institutions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Twelfth Letter bases the new communal autonomy on the secularisation of the national idea, its separation from the religious idea, with elected councils in place of the old religious community.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Dubnow rejects the attempt to make economic factors supreme in history as an error of historical materialism and holds that the decisive factor for a nation's destiny is its spiritual force, not its external power.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Twelfth Letter calls freedom of language and autonomy of the school the most important national rights, and the Fourth claims the right to use one's language in all social institutions and as the language of instruction.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Fourth Letter states that a minority forming the majority in its own province requires regional autonomy where it is settled, while a dispersed minority needs communal and cultural autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Fourth Letter wants Jewish religious communities turned into secular national communities, with the religious label removed from secular institutions, negating the supremacy of religion.

national-church-status.rationale: Dubnow treats the principle of a ruling church as one history has discarded and condemns the religious unitarism that brought inquisitions and religious wars.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Fourth Letter says a dispersed Jewish nationality cannot seek territorial or political separation but only social and cultural autonomy: its own language, schools and communities inside the states where it lives.

national-mission.rationale: Dubnow says he is removed from any doctrine of a predetermined national mission and grounds a nation's existence in self-determination rather than a mission to others.

national-rebirth.rationale: Dubnow calls assimilation national suicide and presents autonomism as the path to the rebirth of the spirit throughout the Diaspora and the renaissance of Judaism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Dubnow grants each nation the right to self-determination but holds that a dispersed nationality can seek only cultural autonomy, not a state, and that history moves toward multinational states.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pinson reports that Dubnow called for Jewish self-defence units during the pogroms and was no follower of Tolstoyan passive resistance.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Dubnow wants the Jewish community secularised, its religious label removed from secular institutions, and rejects treating the Jews as fragments broken up into religious sects rather than a nationality.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Eleventh Letter says various political, social and class parties can and must exist inside the nation, and the Folkspartei programme rests on a democratic constitution.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Dubnow welcomed the Jewish part in the revolution against tsarist absolutism as the necessary reaction of an oppressed people and backed armed self-defence against pogroms.

population-transfer.rationale: In 1939 Dubnow called for a fight against the plans to expel millions of Jews from the countries they helped build and against the Hitler expulsions.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Dubnow defines the aim of autonomism as preserving the national type and perfecting it, and calls the defence of national individuality a necessary condition of human freedom.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Dubnow opposed schemes to 'emancipate' Jews out of the countries where they were citizens and wanted them to keep their civic rights where they lived.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Tenth Letter wants the masses re-educated in the spirit of a state based on law in place of the law of the fist, and the Fourth seeks freedom within a state built on law and justice.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dubnow demands that Jews hold all civic and political rights together with their national rights, without renouncing one for the other.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Tenth Letter condemns the tsarist rules that confined Jews to the Pale of Settlement and drove them into crowded cities as an inquisition, and the programme demands full equal rights.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Third Letter faults rationalism and positivism for forgetting the world of mystery where religion reigns and counts religion part of creative spiritual culture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 1939 Dubnow called for a struggle against 'the guardians of the closed gates' in the countries of immigration, and the Thirteenth Letter treats emigration as a lifeline for the persecuted.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Fourth Letter calls autonomy the firm and inalienable right of each national individuality, its limits to be fixed by law and recognised in international law.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dubnow says autonomists believe in an evolutionary Judaism that adjusts to new cultural conditions, and in 1939 that the core of Judaism can be preserved only by adjusting to modern life.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Third Letter says those who see religion as a destructive force to be rooted out were misled, and that purified religion will be an ethical force in the scientific age, though Dubnow expects the national idea to be secularised.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Dubnow holds that one may be a Jew according to the Talmud, Maimonides, Mendelssohn, the Besht, Geiger or Hirsch, and in 1939 that no party may claim a monopoly of Judaism.

religious-nation.rationale: Dubnow separates the national idea from religion and defines Jewry as a cultural-historical nation, though he also holds that conversion to Christianity means leaving the Jewish nation.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Dubnow's 1939 letter calls the Nazi expulsions a plague to be fought, and the Third Letter condemns any nationality that suppresses another's free individuality.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Tenth Letter praises those who joined the Jewish self-defence and paid with their lives as fulfilling their duty to their fellow men, and the Twelfth vows to fight for freedom to the end.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Fourth Letter treats the old isolated community as a one-sided thesis to be overcome in a new synthesis, and in 1939 Dubnow said progressive Jews will never return to the medieval ghetto.

revive-national-language.rationale: Dubnow saw no hope of making Hebrew the daily language of the Diaspora and defended Yiddish and Russian, but hailed its revival in Palestine's schools; his texts go both ways.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Twelfth Letter concentrates the work on securing civic and national rights in the Diaspora because a Zionist state seems impossible, while also making organised emigration a national task.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Dubnow refuses to break the chain that joins the nation's present to its past and wants the synthesis to keep the best of the inherited tradition.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Tenth Letter condemns police, soldiers and Cossacks for joining the 1905 pogroms and the new government for failing to bring the murderers to justice.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dubnow welcomes the passing of the ruling church in the free state as the model for ending the ruling nationality, and wants communal institutions separated from religion.

single-official-language.rationale: The Third Letter condemns the nationalism of ruling nations that forces minorities to adopt its language and schools, and Dubnow defended Yiddish, Hebrew and Russian alike as instruments of Jewish culture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Dubnow's programme demands a democratic constitution and a state founded on law and justice, which leaves no room for a ruler above the law.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Dubnow describes the Jews as a spiritual nation and, through the Pharisees, praises politics that seeks inner social and spiritual progress rather than brute force.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Dubnow called for Jewish self-defence units during the tsarist pogroms and condemned the police and army for being allowed to destroy them.

state-harmful.rationale: Dubnow describes the state as the outer social organisation that protects its members' needs and seeks the freedom of national groups within a state based on law and justice, not the state's abolition.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Dubnow keeps religion in the storehouse of national culture and warns that whoever seeks to destroy it undermines the basis of national existence.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In 1939 Dubnow insisted that no party may claim a monopoly of Judaism and that the free competition of ideas must continue, and the Eleventh Letter says many parties must exist inside the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pinson writes that Dubnow strenuously opposed any national oppression or national expansionism, and the Third Letter condemns aggressive nationalism that seeks dominion over others.

total-state.rationale: The Fourth Letter says broad autonomy is possible where government does not interfere in citizens' private lives and there is no authoritarian rule or excessive concentration of power, and in 1935 Dubnow called the return to political unitarism the worst plague of the time.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Pinson reports that Dubnow opposed Bolshevism as void of ethics and debasing the human being, condemned fascism and Nazism as murderous, and in 1935 called the 'black-red insanity' a catastrophe.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Dubnow presents Jewish history as an unbroken chain of autonomy from the ancient state to the modern communities, and the Jews as a nation that has never ceased to exist.

unions-good.rationale: The Tenth Letter calls the workers' economic struggle against capitalists, waged through trade unions, strikes and pressure on parliaments, a defence of their just interests that will go on until their rights are fully recognised, while rejecting class politics that divides the nation.

universal-morality.rationale: Dubnow grounds national ethics in an objective standard of justice and the equal worth of all nations, and in 1935 appealed to human conscience and the categorical imperative.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Third Letter calls the militarism born of wars between national egotisms a plague of the time and says Jewish nationalism has nothing in common with any tendency towards violence.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Fourth Letter tells Jews to abandon watchful waiting for a programme of action and unceasing war for human and national rights, and the Eleventh makes national politics the supreme duty of an oppressed people.

workers-nation.rationale: The Tenth and Eleventh Letters demand that Jewish workers' parties fight under a Jewish national banner and reject leaders who tell the Jewish worker that his interests with a foreign proletariat outweigh those he shares with his own people.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: The Tenth Letter says the democratic programme leaves room for the Socialists' minimum demands and that they can cooperate with the democrats until those are won, and counts pressure on parliaments for pro-labour laws among the workers' legitimate means.

missingStatements.text: A nation can survive as a people through its culture, history and institutions without possessing a territory or state of its own.
missingStatements.rationale: Dubnow's theory of a spiritual nation that has passed beyond the tribal and territorial-political stages is the doctrine's core, and no statement states it directly.

missingStatements.text: Members of a national minority should be guaranteed collective rights, such as a legal national assembly, in addition to equal individual rights.
missingStatements.rationale: Autonomists held that Jews should hold rights both as individuals and as members of their national groups, and the Folkspartei sought a Russia-wide Jewish national assembly.

missingStatements.text: A people's culture is best preserved if it develops in a language its people actually speak, rather than in a revived ancient one.
missingStatements.rationale: Autonomists stressed Yiddish, the living language of Eastern European Jewry, as the instrument of national culture.

missingStatements.text: A persecuted people should organise emigration to new centres as one of its national tasks.
missingStatements.rationale: Dubnow makes organised emigration to America and Palestine part of the national programme alongside the fight for rights at home, a position no statement captures.

quotes.text: Our task is not to hinder but to organize this mighty migration
include the organization of emigration among our national tasks

notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-10), bringing a pre-rules audit up to rules 5. The first pass rested on Wikipedia and two short encyclopedia entries; this pass read Dubnow's own Letters on Old and New Judaism in full English translation (Nationalism and History, archive.org), his 1939 letter and Pinson's introductory essay, and rewrote or nulled every earlier answer (reviewHistory keeps them); the three earlier missing statements, already added to the bank, are now cited to the Letters and Pinson, which state them. Earlier answers that rested on Wikipedia, on autonomism's general aims or on what adherents would probably think were nulled (159). Themes searched in the full text: government (democracy, constitution, parties, parliament, rule of law, autonomy and its guarantees), liberty and rights (equal rights, group rights, language, schools), society and culture (religion and secularism, assimilation, tradition, education, continuity), means (revolution, self-defence, gradualism, organisation), world (Zionism, Palestine, emigration, expansionism, militarism, totalitarianism), and economy (class struggle, unions, socialism, property, trade), where the Letters say little beyond rejecting class politics; ecology, technology, gender and family, crime and most economic policy are not discussed at all. Not reached: the YIVO Encyclopedia articles (a script-only page that returns no text) and Gechtman's article on Érudit (bot check). The Encyclopaedia Judaica entries on Autonomism, Dubnow and the Folkspartei (s2, s4 and encyclopedia.com's Folkspartei entry) were read but are not cited for current answers: they call the doctrine 'Autonomism', which in this catalog is the name of a different ideology, so the source check cannot tie them to Jewish Autonomism by name. Over time: Dubnow grew more receptive to Palestine (the 1937 preface says he opposed only Zionism's denial of the Diaspora); answers follow the Letters, his mature statement. Contested points: he rejects class politics but accepts workers' economic struggle (class-collaboration 0), demands all rights at once yet works step by step (gradual-change, small-step-social-reform 0), ranks national types by stage while affirming the equal worth of nations (cultures-equal-different 0), and declined to make Hebrew the Diaspora's language while welcoming its revival in Palestine (revive-national-language 0).
